function: Downlink channel estimation and CSI feedback: ResNet-DQ de-quantizer, unfolded GMMV-LAMP estimator with learned wideband dictionaries, and CSI-ResNet autoencoder compressing CSI to bits (pp. 1, 5).
system: mmWave UM-MIMO downlink: AP with 128 antennas (256, 512 also), 2 RF chains, hybrid ULA; single-antenna UEs, 2-bit ADCs; 70 GHz, 10 GHz bandwidth; no RIS (pp. 4, 10).
method: Data-driven ResNet-DQ and CSI-ResNet autoencoder plus knowledge-driven GMMV-LAMP (unfolded AMP with trainable parameters and data-driven dictionary); supervised NMSE losses, trained module by module; Adam (pp. 9-10).
data_channel: Own simulated Saleh-Valenzuela-based far-, near- and hybrid-field datasets: 150,000 training and 30,000 test samples; random AoD, delay, scatterer positions; no standardized or measured channel (pp. 5, 10).
test_conditions: Training and validation sets have identical features; SNR swept -10 to 10 dB; Fig. 16 trains on far-field, mixed or hybrid data, tests hybrid-field (pp. 10, 13).
baselines: Non-learned: GMMV-AMP and SOMP [17], polar-domain codebook [63]. Learned: MMV-LAMP [20], CSI-Net [31] (pp. 11-15).
metrics: De-quantization, estimation and reconstruction NMSE (dB) versus SNR; feedback bits; complexity orders (pp. 10-15).
complexity: Big-O orders for test stage in Table III: proposed GMMV-LAMP O((GVK+K^2)T+G N_AP K) versus GMMV-AMP, MMV-LAMP, SOMP; no runtime or parameter counts; ResNet-DQ and CSI-ResNet not covered (pp. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 5: "Saleh-Valenzuela channel model [55]" is the base of the channel; p. 10: "near-field, and hybrid near- and far- field scenarios, we generate" own datasets. Custom simulator, textbook model; no TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "other two cases are clearly attributed to the model mismatch of" the purely far-field and purely near-field CSI; Fig. 16 trains on far-field only or mixed near/far data and evaluates in the hybrid near- and far-field scenario.
q3_support: p. 11: "The benchmark MMV-LAMP network [20] assumes" identical pilots and a frequency-flat DFT WRD; it is the learned baseline in the NMSE comparison of Fig. 12, where the non-learned GMMV-AMP is also plotted (p. 12: "the GMMV-AMP [17] suffers from slow convergence and has"; SOMP in Table II). p. 15: "benchmark CSI-Net [31] outputs floating-point-number vectors," is the learned feedback baseline (NMSE, Fig. 21).
q4_support: p. 13: Table III lists "Proposed GMMV-LAMP with T layers" with order O((GV K + K^2)T + G N_AP K), next to GMMV-AMP, MMV-LAMP and SOMP; p. 12: "we focus on the computational complexity in the testing stage". Orders only, for the estimator.
q5_support: p. 10: "samples are 150000 and 30000, respectively" are self-generated training and test samples; no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data anywhere in the paper.
notes: PDF is arXiv:2403.12813v1 (19 Mar 2024), 'Knowledge and Data Dual-Driven Channel Estimation and Feedback for Ultra-Massive MIMO Systems under Hybrid Field Beam Squint Effect' (Wang, Gao, Chen, Ning, Chen, Su, Wang, Poor); the DOI is not printed in the text. Area 2: estimation and feedback of the channel. q4 covers only the GMMV-LAMP estimator, not ResNet-DQ or CSI-ResNet. q2 rests on the Fig. 16 train-test mismatch (far-field or mixed training, hybrid-field test). Learned baselines: MMV-LAMP [20] (earlier model-driven network) for estimation and CSI-Net [31] for feedback.
